value.body: Under the National Health Mission (NHM), state and district health societies hire Ayush medical officers — BAMS, BHMS, BUMS or BSMS graduates — on contract, mainly for Ayush wings in primary health centres, community health centres and district hospitals. These posts are separate from the regular posts that state Ayush departments fill through public service commissions.

items.label: Type of post
items.note: Often about 11 months to a year, renewable on performance and funding

items.label: Pay
items.note: Set by each state; no common national pay scale

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BAMS, BHMS, BUMS or BSMS degree with completed internship and permanent registration with the state board or council for Indian medicine / homoeopathy (provisional registration is often not accepted). States advertise on their NHM or district websites; selection is by walk-in interview, merit list or a written test, depending on the state.

value.title: At a glance
items: Contract posts do not carry the tenure and pension of regular government service.
Remuneration and renewal terms differ between states and can change with the yearly NHM budget.
Rural postings and knowledge of the local language are commonly expected.
Regular Ayush medical officer posts are filled separately by state public service commissions.
